prompt: Read a rectangular 2D array in clockwise spiral order -- across the top, down the right side, back along the bottom, up the left side, then inward -- and return the values as a 1D array.
explanation: Four boundary indices (top, bottom, left, right) describe the untraversed rectangle; each pass copies one edge and moves its boundary inward. The two guarded passes (bottom row and left column) are the classic trap: after the top row and right column of a single-row or single-column ring are consumed, the boundaries may have crossed, and re-walking the same cells would duplicate them. Checking top <= bottom and left <= right before those passes prevents that.
hints: Maintain top, bottom, left, right boundaries and loop while top <= bottom && left <= right.
Each ring is four for loops: top row left-to-right, right column top-to-bottom, bottom row right-to-left, left column bottom-to-top; move the matching boundary after each.
Before walking the bottom row re-check top <= bottom, and before the left column re-check left <= right -- otherwise a single row or column gets read twice.
